title: Healthcare
question: Who should pay for health care in the United States, and how should that care be organized?
summary: A narrow starting question: who pays the bill for health care, and what happens when the answer is a family, an employer, an insurer, or the government.
sourceNote: Further reading only. This outline does not take facts from these pages yet. When the full page is written, government or other primary sources will be cited first, and the Just Facts page will stay linked as further reading. The wording on this site will stay original. No statistics are included here.

paragraphs: This section will explain, in everyday words, the main ways Americans pay for doctors and hospitals: a family pays directly, an employer plan, a private insurer, or a government program. The full page will start with that question instead of trying to cover all of medicine.
No statistics will be added until they are checked against primary sources.

This section will name the disagreement over whether health care works better as a shared government guarantee or as a market where people shop for insurance and care. It will treat cost, access, and the freedom to choose a doctor as separate goals that can collide.

sides.intro: Each column will hold one side’s strongest fair case, in plain language and at similar length. Neither case is written yet.

a.title: One side’s strongest case
paragraphs: This column will give the strongest fair case for one view, using checked facts. It will not use insults, and it is not written yet.

b.title: The other side’s strongest case
paragraphs: This column will give the strongest fair case for the other view, under the same rules. It is not written yet.
This section will look for aims people share: being able to see a doctor when they are sick, not being ruined by one bill, and not wasting money on care that does not help.

items: The questions will ask who should bear a risk that is rare but huge, and what a patient gives up when someone else pays the bill.

sources.title: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
